content:
Nuevo Laredo's traditional Student Sports Week returns November 9 through 13, bringing together students from preschool through university to represent their schools in eight sports, according to the municipal government.

The week-long competition, which the city says has more than five decades of history, is organized by the municipal government through the Secretariat of Education, Culture and Sports, the report said.

Competitions are planned in chess, track and field, basketball, baseball, soccer, volleyball, flag football and frontón, with categories from preschool to university, according to the report. Preschool children as young as 3 can compete in track and field, while university students up to 27 years and 11 months old can participate under the call's requirements.

Events will be held at the Unidad Deportiva Benito Juárez and the Centro de Alto Rendimiento at the Ciudad Deportiva, with activities distributed by sport and category, the report said. The chess tournament is scheduled for Friday, November 13.

Schools interested in taking part must go to the Directorate of Physical Culture and Sports at the Unidad Deportiva Benito Juárez to obtain the registration form and learn the participation requirements, according to the report. Documents are received from 8:00 a.m. to 9:00 p.m., and schools must present their students' registration and documentation endorsed by each campus director. More information is available by phone at 867 719 4782 and through the Secretariat of Education, Culture and Sports' official social media accounts.
